status: Original two-product manufacturing assessment programme using unchanged claims; historical components retained without treating them as complete impact analysis.

paper-process.publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada, 2017 sector account
paper-process.readScope: Actual complete main sector/process/risk-instrument body read; no linked regulation text or images claimed.
paper-process.fact: Fibre inputs include residual wood/chips and recovered paper. Water, heat and chemicals are used in paper manufacture; fuel/byproduct energy and wastewater treatment are part of the account. Printing, packaging and tissue are identified products.
paper-process.limits: The general sector account does not establish every individual mill process, current fuel mix or zero pollution; do not copy its broad cellulose wording into a molecular reaction claim.

paper-water.publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada, 2026 overview
paper-water.readScope: Actual main overview, scope and requirements read. Legal page links not treated as fully read regulations.
paper-water.fact: Mill effluent can threaten fish, habitat and people who consume fish. Limits and monitoring address oxygen-demanding matter, suspended solids and lethal effluent.
paper-water.limits: Regulation is a mitigation instrument, not proof every mill complies or every receiving water is harmless. No legal advice, current numeric limit or claim that all contamination has ended.

aluminium-process.publisher: US Energy Information Administration, dated 9 May 2014
aluminium-process.readScope: Actual entire article main body read; graphs not visually checked.
aluminium-process.fact: The primary route goes from bauxite through alumina to smelted aluminium. A secondary route prepares, melts and refines scrap, including used beverage cans, and requires substantially less production energy in the selected comparison.
aluminium-process.limits: Historical US account; no production share, exact energy percentage, capital-cost percentage or current Canadian numerical claim is required. Recyclability does not prove that every discarded can is actually collected or reprocessed.

aluminium-emissions.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency, February 2026 page with historical partnership context
aluminium-emissions.readScope: Complete actual main body including process, mitigation and FAQ read; linked technical publications/media not reviewed.
aluminium-emissions.fact: Certain primary smelting disruptions produce potent greenhouse gases. Monitoring, employee training and adjusted alumina feeding can reduce those disruptions; avoiding them also reduces wasted inputs.
aluminium-emissions.limits: No chemical-formula/GWP/technical electrolysis inventory, claim all emissions disappear, or universal emission factor. The page contains differing historical GWP numbers, which are deliberately excluded.

paper.product: Ordinary printing paper, tissue or a paper box
paper.process: Prepare fibre and make paper using water/heat/selected chemicals, then convert/transport the usable product; collect/treat manufacturing wastewater as described in the sector account.
paper.environment: Wastewater can consume dissolved oxygen or carry suspended material, affecting fish/habitat. Manufacturing heat also requires a chosen energy source; no generic renewable=harmless inference.
paper.society: Useful printing, packaging and tissue products meet everyday needs. The documented threat through fish consumption connects water protection to people as well as aquatic organisms. It is a threat/mitigation relationship, not a diagnosis that a named community is harmed.
paper.societyAction: Mills manage treatment and monitor effects; public rules and reporting can require limits/remedial action. Explain how these act on the actual discharge pathway rather than treating regulation as instant recovery.
paper.individualAction: Avoid unnecessary sheets/packaging, reuse suitable paper and follow the actual local collection guidance. Reducing demand and supplying recoverable fibre differ from treating mill effluent; an individual does not operate the industrial plant.
paper.tradeoff: A recycled-fibre label alone does not prove no water/energy demand or pollution. A manufacturing decision must also meet the product purpose and actual treatment/energy constraints.

aluminium.product: A beverage can or other clearly specified aluminium product
aluminium.material: Bauxite-derived metal versus appropriately collected aluminium scrap
aluminium.process: Compare the ore→alumina→metal route with sorted/prepared scrap→melt/refine→usable metal. Keep collection, material processing and product making distinct.
aluminium.environment: The selected secondary route needs substantially less production energy. Primary smelting can emit potent greenhouse gases during process disruptions; changing energy demand and reducing those disruptions address distinct pathways.
aluminium.society: Manufacture provides useful containers/materials. More efficient operation avoids wasted energy/material inputs and can reduce production costs; this is not proof of a particular shop price, job total or universal community benefit.
aluminium.societyAction: Producers can monitor and adjust operations, train staff and provide suitable collection/reprocessing systems; relevant institutions can support collection/standards. Explain the mechanism and an actual limit instead of simply saying recycle.
aluminium.individualAction: Use only packaging needed for the task, reuse an appropriate alternative where suitable and place accepted cans into the verified collection stream. Collection is one step; sorting and actual reprocessing are still required.
aluminium.tradeoff: Scrap must be collected and suitable for the process; no zero-energy/zero-emission claim follows. Compare the same intended product/service and identify missing suitability, transport or safety facts.
